body_ar:
كرم الله المرأة وأعطاها حقوقاً تتمتع بها، وشرفها بأن جعل نفقتها ومؤنتها على الرجل، وصانها بالبقاء في بيتها، وبالحجاب وعدم الاختلاط بالرجال، ثم جاءت جاهلية الغرب فاتخذت من المرأة سلعة تباع، ومن عفافها تجارة ووسيلة للإفساد ونشر الرذيلة، وهذا مما يوجب على الداعية المسلم أن ينورالأمة ويذكرها بخيرية الإسلام وصيانته للمرأة، وما عليه دعاة الغرب من الرذيلة والفواحش.
تكريم المرأة بين الجاهلية والإسلام:
الحمد لله، والصلاة والسلام على رسول الله، أما بعد: فإن موضوع المرأة أصبح من الموضوعات التي ينبغي أن يهتم بها الرجال والنساء في عصرنا هذا خصوصاً، لما أشاعه أعداء الإسلام فيه من الافتراءات وما روجوا فيه من الشبهات التي كان العالم في غنى عنها لولا هذه الترويجات المغرضة. وذلك أن المرأة لا تتميز على غيرها من خلق الله تعالى إلا تميزاً بسيطاً فسيولوجياً هو الذي جعلها امرأة، وهذا التميز لا يقتضي أن تفرد بكلام، أو أن تفرد بتفكير، أو أن يكون لها وضع مستقل، فهي من خلق الله تعالى...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God honoured woman and gave her rights that she enjoys. He ennobled her by placing her maintenance and her upkeep upon the man, and safeguarded her by her remaining in her house, by the covering (ḥijāb) and by her not mixing with men. Then came the ignorance of the West, which made of woman a commodity to be sold, and of her chastity a trade and a means of corruption and of spreading vice. This makes it incumbent upon the Muslim who calls people to God to enlighten the community and to remind it of the goodness of Islam and of its safeguarding of woman, and of the vice and the indecencies that the callers of the West stand upon.

## The honouring of woman, between the age of ignorance and Islam

Praise belongs to God, and blessing and peace upon the Messenger of God. To proceed: the subject of woman has become one of the subjects that men and women ought to concern themselves with in this age of ours in particular, because of the fabrications that the enemies of Islam have spread about it and the specious arguments they have promoted in it — of which the world had no need, but for this tendentious promotion. For woman is not distinguished from the rest of God's creation, exalted is He, except by a simple physiological distinction, the one that made her a woman. And this distinction does not require that she be singled out for a discourse of her own, or singled out for a thinking of her own, or that she have a standing of her own; for she is of God's creation, exalted is He …

flags.arabic: وهذا التميز لا يقتضي أن تفرد بكلام، أو أن تفرد بتفكير، أو أن يكون لها وضع مستقل، فهي من خلق الله تعالى
flags.context: the Sheikh's own opening argument, at the point where the text breaks off
options: does not require that she be singled out for a discourse of her own, or … a thinking of her own, or that she have a standing of her own
does not mean she should be given separate treatment, separate thought, or an independent position
does not entail that she be set apart in discussion, in reasoning, or in status
flags.note: THE passage in this slice that most needs a scholar's eye, because the served text stops in the middle of it and two opposite readings remain open. The sentence says that the only distinction between woman and the rest of God's creation is physiological, and that this distinction does not require that she be 'singled out' in three respects. Read one way — and the closing clause 'for she is of God's creation' supports this — it is an argument against treating woman as a separate category at all: a refusal of 'the woman question' as such, on the ground of common humanity. Read another way it could be taken to deny her any distinct standing in law. The Arabic verb 'تفرد' is neutral between being set apart in her favour and being set apart against her, and the text breaks off before the Sheikh says which he means. The translation has been kept deliberately neutral — 'singled out', 'a standing of her own' — so that it does not decide what he left unsaid. It must not be published without the full text behind the download, and preferably not without the Sheikh's office confirming the sense. Style guide sections 6, 10 and 12 all apply.

flags.note: Beyond the usual two-voice problem, in this record the two voices pull in different directions and a reader who takes them as one will misread both. The site's synopsis is a polemic: it lists specific rulings about a woman's place, characterises the West as a new age of ignorance, and calls on preachers to answer it. The Sheikh's transcribed opening does something else — it says the subject has been inflated by fabrications, and then argues that woman is not a separate category of God's creation at all. Nothing in the transcribed portion states any of the specific rulings in the synopsis. If this record is displayed, the separation must be unmistakable, and nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as the Sheikh's.

flags.arabic: وصانها بالبقاء في بيتها، وبالحجاب وعدم الاختلاط بالرجال
options: safeguarded her by her remaining in her house, by the covering (ḥijāb) and by her not mixing with men
protected her through her staying at home, veiling, and segregation from men
flags.note: Three specific and much-contested rulings, stated as settled, in a paragraph written by the site and not by the Sheikh. Style guide section 12 applies squarely: translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened, with the decision to publish left to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. 'حجاب' is rendered 'the covering' with the Arabic in brackets rather than 'the veil', which in English now names a face covering specifically and would narrow the term. 'عدم الاختلاط' is rendered 'her not mixing with men', which is what the Arabic says; 'segregation' imports an institutional frame the Arabic does not have.

flags.context: the closing sentence of the site's synopsis
options: preserve the missing space in body_ar and translate the evident words
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. 'ينور الأمة' is served as one word, 'ينورالأمة'. The same class of spacing artefact appears at record 707 of this slice and again at record 717. Preserved in body_ar and not repaired.

'جاهلية' is the term for the pre-Islamic age of ignorance, and applying it to a contemporary society is a deliberate and loaded move with a specific twentieth-century history behind it. Left in plain English so that an English reader meets the claim as an Arabic reader does, rather than being shielded from it by a transliteration. The section heading uses the same word of the pre-Islamic period, and the English renders it 'the age of ignorance' there, so the parallel the source draws stays visible.

'شبهة' is an argument with enough apparent force to mislead, not a doubt in the mind of the person who holds it. 'Doubts' would make the sentence about a psychological state; the Sheikh is describing what he says has been circulated by others.

translator_notes: One of a run of nine records, IDs 725-733, in the Islamic-thought section, all uploaded on 10 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lecture, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/g-* series, numbered g-16 to g-24 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lecture was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The most editorially sensitive record in this slice, and the one whose display decision should be taken deliberately rather than by default. It is flagged critical_for_display on two independent grounds: the served text stops mid-argument, and its two voices make different arguments.

This record and record 726 carry the same upload timestamp in their aliases, 10 May 2011 at 10:22:11, which is further evidence that the whole run is a bulk upload and that the dates say nothing about when the lectures were given.
'المرأة' with the generic article is rendered 'woman' rather than 'the woman' or 'women', which is how the Arabic generic works and how the title reads.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record. The specific rulings in the synopsis are stated without any grading term attached.
